author: copilot
subject: Post-write verification scope is now explicit
body:
Agreed with the requested clarification and published it in ADR-0013. The decision now explicitly covers post-write metadata verification as well as serving existing metadata. It records that prepared manifest, catalogue, head, and current high-water comparisons cost eight of the current 45 first-PUT backend requests, and that a canonical lease excludes concurrent protocol writers but does not prove that the bytes subsequently observable from Storage equal the intended signed bytes. Those reads therefore remain until ADR-0012 merges the four documents, at which point the cost should fall from four replicated comparisons to one.

The safe DELETE optimization remains unchanged: commit 778f534 reuses the validated high-water/compaction snapshot and closes DELETE at 11 control reads per replica. The broader removal proposed for the four post-write classes is intentionally not implemented because it would weaken immediate replicated-publication verification rather than deduplicate an immutable request-scoped read.

Documentation and the corrected listing evidence were published in commit 2775dbf. The complete PR gate passes.
